title: Akhni (Chittagong and Sylhet spiced beef and rice)

ingredients.name: beef or mutton on the bone, cut into pieces
basmati rice, washed and soaked 20 minutes

steps: Heat half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the onions until deep golden; take out a third for garnish.
Add the whole spices, ginger and garlic paste and fry for a minute, then add the meat and brown it for 8 minutes.
Stir in the yoghurt, chilli, turmeric and salt and cook until the oil separates from the masala.
Add 1 cup of hot water, cover and simmer until the meat is nearly tender, about 40 minutes.
Add the drained rice, the remaining hot water (enough to cover the rice by about 1.5 cm), the green chillies and the rest of the ghee.
Cook uncovered until the water is absorbed, then cover tightly and steam on the lowest heat for 15 minutes.
Fluff, scatter the reserved onions over the top and serve with salad.

title: Bakarkhani (Old Dhaka spiced layered bread)
steps: Mix the flour, salt and sugar and rub in 3 tablespoons of ghee, then add the milk and enough water to make a stiff dough and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide into balls and roll each into a thin circle, brush with ghee and fold into a layered shape, roll into a thicker round.
Prick lightly, brush with milk (with saffron if using) and sprinkle with poppy seeds.
Bake at 200 C for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and crisp on the outside.
Cool slightly and serve with tea or curry.

title: Beef Satkara (Sylheti beef curry with citrus)

ingredients.name: satkara (or 1 grapefruit/lemon and a little lime), cut into pieces, with pith and peel left on

steps: Fry the onions in the oil until golden, then add the ginger and garlic pastes and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the beef, turmeric, chilli powder, cumin, coriander and salt and fry over high heat for 10 minutes.
Pour in the water, cover and simmer for 1 to 1.5 hours until the beef is tender.
Add the green chillies and the citrus pieces, plus a squeeze of their juice, and cook for 10 minutes more.
Serve with plain rice, eating a little of the citrus rind with each bite if you like its bitterness.

title: Beguni (Bengali battered fried aubergine)

ingredients.name: medium aubergines, sliced into thin rounds

steps: Whisk the gram flour, rice flour, turmeric, chilli powder, nigella seeds and salt with the water into a smooth, medium-thick batter.
Salt the aubergine slices lightly and pat dry.
Heat oil in a deep pan to medium-hot.
Dip each aubergine slice in the batter, let the excess drip off and lower it into the oil.
Fry in batches, turning, for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp, then drain on paper.
Serve hot with puffed rice or with khichuri.

title: Bhapa Pitha (steamed rice flour cakes with coconut and date-palm jaggery)

ingredients.name: date-palm jaggery (khejur gur), or brown sugar

steps: Mix the rice flour with the salt and warm water to a damp crumbly mixture and rub through a sieve.
Mix the coconut with the jaggery and cardamom for the filling.
Spoon a layer of the flour into a small cup mould, make a hollow, add a spoon of filling, then cover with more flour.
Steam over boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes until cooked through and the flour is set.
Unmould carefully and serve warm.

title: Borhani (spicy Bangladeshi yoghurt drink)
steps: Whisk the yoghurt and water until smooth and thin.
Grind the mint, coriander, chillies and mustard to a paste with a pinch of salt.
Stir the paste, cumin, black salt, pepper, salt and sugar into the yoghurt.
Chill for at least 30 minutes.
Serve cold in glasses, traditionally with biryani.

title: Chingri Malai Curry (prawns in coconut milk)
steps: Marinate the prawns with salt and a pinch of turmeric for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil and fry the prawns briefly for 1 to 2 minutes until just pink, then set aside.
In the same oil fry the bay leaves, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves, then add the onion and ginger and cook until golden.
Add the remaining turmeric, chilli powder and sugar, then pour in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Return the prawns and green chillies and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until they are cooked through.
Stir in the ghee and serve with steamed rice.

title: Chitoi Pitha (Bangladeshi steamed-style rice cakes)

ingredients.name: date-palm jaggery syrup or milk-based molasses sauce, to serve

steps: Whisk the rice flour, plain flour, salt and sugar with the water into a thin, smooth batter and rest it for 30 minutes.
Heat a clay or heavy pitha mould (or a small non-stick pan) and grease it lightly.
Pour a small ladle of batter into the mould, cover and cook on low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until spongy and set.
Slide out and repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve warm with date-palm jaggery syrup or with a savoury curry.

title: Chomchom (Bengali syrup-soaked cheese sweet)

ingredients.name: grated khoa or desiccated coconut, to coat

steps: Boil the milk, add the lemon juice to curdle it, drain the curds in a cloth and rinse under cold water.
Hang for 30 minutes, then knead the chhena with the flour for about 8 minutes until smooth.
Shape into oval cylinders about 5 cm long.
Boil the sugar and water with cardamom to make a light syrup and gently simmer the shaped chhena in the syrup, covered, for 15 to 20 minutes until they swell.
Cool them in the syrup, then roll in grated khoa or coconut and serve chilled.

title: Chotpoti (Dhaka tangy chickpea street snack)

ingredients.name: dried white peas or chickpeas, soaked overnight
crushed fried puffed puris (or crisps), to top

steps: Boil the soaked peas with the turmeric and salt until soft and mushy, adding the potatoes for the last 10 minutes.
Mash lightly so the mixture is thick but not completely smooth.
Stir in the tamarind pulp, cumin and chaat masala and simmer for 5 minutes.
Divide among bowls and top with the chopped egg, onion, green chilli and coriander.
Scatter crushed puris or crisps over the top and serve right away.

title: Duck Bamboo Curry (Sylheti duck with bamboo shoots)
steps: Trim excess fat from the duck and pat dry.
Heat the oil, fry the onions until golden, then add the ginger and garlic pastes.
Add the duck and brown for 10 minutes, stirring in the turmeric, chilli, cumin and salt.
Add the water, cover and simmer for 40 minutes.
Stir in the bamboo shoots and green chillies and cook for 20 to 25 minutes until the duck is tender and the gravy is thick.
Skim any excess fat from the surface and serve with rice.

title: Durus (Chittagong whole chicken curry)
steps: Fry the onions in the oil until golden brown, add the cinnamon and cardamom, then the ginger and garlic pastes, and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken, turmeric, chilli, cumin, coriander and salt and fry until the chicken is lightly browned, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the yoghurt and cook until the oil separates.
Pour in the water, cover and simmer for about 30 minutes until the chicken is tender and the broth is thick.
Add the green chillies and simmer 5 more minutes.
Serve with rice or paratha.

title: Jhalmuri (spicy Bengali puffed rice snack)
steps: Combine the onion, tomato, cucumber, chillies, peanuts and coriander in a large bowl.
Add the mustard oil, chaat masala, chilli powder, salt and tamarind or lemon juice and mix well.
Add the puffed rice just before serving and toss quickly so it stays crisp.
Serve immediately in paper cones or bowls.

title: Kala Bhuna (Chittagong dark roasted beef curry)
steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the onions until very dark brown, being careful not to burn them, then lift out half and set aside.
Add the whole spices and dried chillies to the oil, then the ginger-garlic paste, and fry until fragrant.
Add the beef, chilli powder, turmeric, cumin, coriander and salt and fry over high heat for 10 minutes.
Add the water and reserved onions, cover and cook on low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender.
Uncover and keep frying on medium-high heat for 15 to 20 minutes until the gravy has dried and the meat is coated in a dark, thick masala, adding the garam masala at the end.
Serve with plain rice or paratha.

title: Ledikeni (Bengali fried cheese balls in syrup)
steps: Curdle the milk with lemon juice, drain the chhena, rinse and press out the water.
Knead the chhena with the flour, semolina, baking powder and cardamom until smooth and soft.
Make a syrup with the sugar and water and keep it warm.
Shape the dough into smooth balls and slightly flatten them.
Fry in hot ghee on low heat until a deep reddish-brown, turning gently.
Transfer immediately to the syrup with the rose water and soak for several hours before serving.

title: Luchi (Bengali deep-fried puffed bread)
steps: Mix the flour and salt, rub in the ghee and add water gradually to make a smooth, firm dough.
Knead for 5 minutes and rest, covered, for 30 minutes.
Divide into small balls and roll each into a round about 10 cm wide.
Heat oil in a deep pan until hot and slide in one round at a time, pressing gently so it puffs up.
Fry for about 30 seconds per side until pale golden, drain on paper and serve hot with potato curry or aloor dom.

title: Machher Jhol (light Bengali fish and potato curry)

ingredients.name: rohu or other firm fish, cut into steaks

steps: Marinate the fish with half the turmeric and salt for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil until hot, fry the fish for about 1 minute per side until lightly golden, then set aside.
In the same oil fry the potato wedges with a pinch of turmeric until just coloured.
Add the nigella seeds, then the tomato, ginger paste, cumin and chilli powder, and cook until soft.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Slide the fish and green chillies back in and simmer gently for 6 to 8 minutes, then finish with coriander and serve with rice.

title: Mishti Doi (Bengali sweet set yoghurt)
steps: Caramelise 1 tablespoon of sugar with the water in a pan until golden brown, then add 1/4 cup of hot milk, stirring until smooth.
Simmer the remaining milk until it reduces to about three-quarters, then add the 1/2 cup sugar and stir to dissolve.
Stir in the caramel and cool the milk to lukewarm, around 40 C.
Whisk in the live yoghurt, then pour into clay pots or a dish.
Cover and keep in a warm place for 6 to 8 hours until set, then chill before serving.

title: Mughlai Paratha (egg and mince stuffed paratha)
steps: Knead the flour, salt, 2 tablespoons oil and water into a soft dough, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Cook the mince with the onion, ginger-garlic paste, cumin and salt until browned and dry, then cool and stir in the chillies, garam masala and coriander.
Beat the eggs, divide into 4 portions and mix a quarter of the mince into each.
Roll a ball of dough very thin, spoon an egg-mince portion onto the centre and fold the edges over to make a closed square parcel.
Fry the parcel in oil on a hot griddle for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and the filling is set.
Repeat with the remaining parcels and serve hot with chutney or pickle.

title: Nunor Bora (Sylheti onion and rice-flour fritters)
steps: Mix the onions, ginger, chillies, coriander, turmeric and salt in a bowl and rub them together lightly so the onion releases some juice.
Add the rice flour and just enough water to form a thick batter that holds together.
Heat oil in a deep pan to medium-hot.
Drop spoonfuls of batter in and fry, turning, for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper and serve hot with chutney or tea.

title: Pantua (Bengali fried cheese dumplings in syrup)
steps: Boil the milk, add the lemon juice to curdle it, drain the curds in muslin and rinse, then hang for 30 minutes.
Knead the drained chhena for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and soft, then knead in the semolina, flour and cardamom.
Shape into small smooth oval balls without cracks.
Make a syrup by boiling the sugar and water for 8 minutes, then stir in the rose water.
Fry the balls in ghee on low heat until deep brown.
Slip the hot balls into the warm syrup and soak for at least 2 hours before serving.

title: Sandesh (Bengali milk fudge sweet)
steps: Boil the milk, curdle it with the lemon juice, drain and rinse the chhena and press out the excess water.
Knead the chhena for 8 to 10 minutes until completely smooth and slightly oily.
Cook it in a non-stick pan over low heat with the sugar and cardamom for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring, until it just comes together as a soft dough.
Cool slightly, press into greased moulds or shape into small discs, and garnish with a pistachio.
Chill until set, then serve.

title: Seven-Colour Tea (Sylheti layered tea)
steps: Brew several separate teas of different strengths, for example a dark, strong black tea sweetened with sugar, a milk tea with condensed milk, a lightly spiced tea with cinnamon and ginger, and a lemon-flavoured tea.
Keep each tea at a different density by adjusting its sugar and milk, so that the heaviest liquids sink and the lightest rise.
Pour the heaviest tea into a tall glass first, then pour each lighter tea slowly over the back of a spoon so they settle in layers.
Serve at once, drinking it layer by layer or stirring the layers together.

title: Shorshe Ilish (hilsa in mustard sauce)

ingredients.name: hilsa steaks (or other oily fish such as mackerel)

steps: Rub the fish with half the turmeric and salt and set aside for 10 minutes.
Grind the soaked mustard seeds with 2 green chillies, a pinch of salt and a little water into a smooth paste.
Heat 2 tablespoons of mustard oil and lightly fry the fish for 1 minute per side, then remove.
Heat the remaining oil, add the nigella seeds and slit chillies, then the mustard paste with the remaining turmeric and the water.
Bring to a gentle simmer, slide the fish into the sauce, cover and cook on low heat for 8 to 10 minutes.
Drizzle a little raw mustard oil over the top and serve with steamed rice.
